description: Square four-post canopy module with a sagging woven tarpaulin sheet lashed over a light steel tube frame, open on all sides.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Square four-post canopy module with a sagging tarpaulin sheet roof lashed down at the corners over a light steel tube frame, four thin steel posts, open on all sides Materials: Woven polypropylene tarpaulin in faded blue with a bright orange underside, creased and sun-brittled with a torn eyelet patched by rope, frayed grommets and stretched tie points, rust-speckled galvanised tube.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.87. 1,888/4,000 triangles, 2/4 draw calls, 2/3 materials, 2/6 unique geometries, two 512 px canvases. The largest opening in the set -- about 240,000 px of enclosed background per frame -- so the turntable runs with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement and a holeviz read per azimuth showing the red over exactly that volume.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope measured 4.000 x 2.700 x 4.000 m off the built module, the tarp owning both cell-edge planes and the frame stopping at 1.998 after the first build's rope collars crossed at 2.002. Four 60 mm tubes at +-1.958, a bottom perimeter rail at 0.11 and NO top rail -- the plate ties the tarp straight to the post heads and the proxy finds a 4.6-5.6% surface band at the bottom of the frame and none at the top.
featureReviews.notes: The absence of a top rail is what makes the sag a four-point catenary rather than a dish, and it is the difference between this bay and every other one in the set.

featureReviews.evidence: A 16 x 16 height grid, 1,152 of the bay's 1,888 triangles: 2.70 at the four ties, 2.49 at the middle of each edge, 2.34 at the centre, with a deterministic fold ripple. The orange lining is the sheet's under-grid and rim colour, thickened to 22 mm so the rim reads at a camera that never sees the underside. Blue measured back at 128-135 against the plate's 118 shaded and 145 lit.
featureReviews.notes: The first build shipped this as a WHITE sail: tintGeo was overwriting the sheet's own two-tone colour attribute with a single hex.

featureReviews.evidence: Round 60 mm tube throughout, rust collars at the four rail joints and the four feet rather than over the whole frame, and a rope collar and hanging knot at each post head. Galvanised tone authored as the inverse of the probed transfer and carried with rust and rope as vertex colours on one material.

name: Tarpaulin Canopy Module
nameTh: หลังคาผ้าใบ
notes: One bay of a modular outdoor roof kit: 4 x 4 m footprint on a 4 m grid, which divides the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles exactly 2 x 2, so a canopy grid lands on the paving grid. Four corner posts, because the brief is a module that includes its own poles and must therefore stand alone; placed side by side the posts pair up at the shared edges, which is what a real market row looks like rather than a defect to design out. Flat rather than pitched, at 2.7 m: a tarp over a tube frame is tensioned, not framed to a slope, and the sag between the four tie points is what makes it read as fabric. That sag has to be real geometry -- a flat quad with a fabric texture reads as painted board -- so the roof wants a shallow subdivided sheet dipping in the middle, which is where this module's triangles should go. Open on all sides. The blue-and-orange woven tarp is the single most recognisable Thai street material in the kit, so the colour is identity and not decoration.
